[[Cologne]] ({{langx|de|Köln}}) is Germany's [[List of cities in Germany with more than 100,000 inhabitants|fourth-largest city]] and the largest city in the Rhineland. As of 31 December 2011, there were officially 1,017,155 residents.<ref>{{cite web |author=Information und Technik NRW |url=http://www.it.nrw.de/statistik/a/daten/amtlichebevoelkerungszahlen/rp3_dez2011.html |title=Bevölkerung im Regierungsbezirk Köln |access-date=2012-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911025756/http://www.it.nrw.de/statistik/a/daten/amtlichebevoelkerungszahlen/rp3_dez2011.html |archive-date=2012-09-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The city is center of the [[Cologne/Bonn Region]] with around 3 million inhabitants (including the neighboring cities of [[Bonn]], [[Hürth]], [[Leverkusen]], and [[Bergisch Gladbach]]).

== Historic population data ==
{{See also|History of Cologne}}

=== Roman Cologne ===
The walls of Colonia Agrippina covered an area of 96.8 hectares,<ref>J.C. Russell, "Late Ancient and Medieval Population," in ''Transactions of the American Philosophical Society'', vol. 48, part 3, table 89.</ref> but the population density within the walls remains uncertain.

=== Medieval Cologne ===
[[File:Nuremberg chronicles - colonia.png|thumb|250px|Woodcut of Cologne from the [[Nuremberg Chronicle]], 1493]]
Since the construction of the Medieval wall in 1180, the area of the old [[Free imperial city|imperial city]] of Cologne has not changed for more than 600 years and was only extended over the old city walls in 1794, just short before the arrival of French troops and Cologne's incorporation into the [[First French Empire]].

=== Modern Cologne ===

==== 16th through 19th century ====
[[File:Köln-und-Deutz-nach-Wenzeslaw-Hollar-von-Prachna-1636.JPG|thumb|250px|Copper engraving of Cologne by Hollar von Prachna, Wenceslaus, 1636]] 
[[File:Blick von Deutz auf die Stadt, Köln ca 1700.jpg|thumb|250px|Coloured drawing of Cologne, ca. 1700]]

After 1815, the [[Kingdom of Prussia]] enforced the construction of fortifications which again hindered any growth for the city. Only with the acquisition of these fortifications in 1881, the city of Cologne had the possibility of a gradual territorial expansion. On 12. November 1883 a strip of territory from parts of the municipalities of [[Ehrenfeld, Cologne|Ehrenfeld]], Kriel, Longerich, Müngersdorf and Rondorf was added to the city. Since 1886, the [[Cologne City Hall|Cologne City Council]] intensified negotiations with the surrounding communities, and on 1 April 1888 ended in a first major incorporation.

==== 20th century ====
The territorial expansion, beginning in the late 19th century, were significant marks for the city's population growth. Major communal reorganizations took place in 1910, 1914, 1922 and 1975.
